flags: Dropped current claims of a 1913 build date, first state highway in three counties, the name Going Round the Horn, and farm stands and cideries lining the road; none is supported by substantive cache text.
Dropped the current 450-foot dune height and description of visitors viewing Glen Lake and running down. The cache supports the Dune Climb location, not those details.

Narrowed the current claim that multiple shanties have been raised since 2020: cache documents the first move in January 2020 and planned subsequent work, not completion. Omitted the unsupported few-surviving-complexes superlative.
The numbered highway is 116.7 miles in its article; the Leelanau byway designation also includes M-109 and M-204. Kept those scopes distinct and omitted an overall byway mileage or driving time.
The cache lacks current manager confirmation for lighthouse tours and National Park Service pass details. The pass note records a cache check only, not live verification.

Sources differ in tribal name ordering: the highway article says Grand Traverse Band of Chippewa and Ottawa Indians; the peninsula article says Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa & Chippewa Indians. No tribal name is used in this draft pending a community source.
